title: Jude and the Typewriter
premise: In 1848, in a river town on the eve of revolution, Jude Marsh, a young compositor apprenticed to typeface cutter Ambrose Sterling, has spent his life believing that history happens elsewhere. When the bridge — the only road out of the valley — closes for the season, Jude is trapped inside the Sterling print workshop alongside Ambrose's daughter Elodie, who has secretly been setting pamphlets for the rebels while her father prints currency for a collapsing regime. When Ambrose is arrested for treason, Jude and Elodie must finish and distribute the one document that could sway the town — a printed record of the soldiers' massacres that the authorities are erasing — before the workshop is seized and the presses destroyed. Jude learns that justice sometimes lives outside the law, that memory can be typeset and made permanent, and that he was never outside history at all; the book ends with the pamphlet in every hand in town, the workshop burned, and Jude and Elodie crossing the thawing bridge into an uncertain but self-authored future.
about_author: Vesper Amberdale is the pen name of a former letterpress printer who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century presses in provincial archives. Their novels explore the people who made history with their hands rather than their names.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes the Sterling workshop's rhythms: sorting type, the smell of ink, Ambrose's exacting standards, and Elodie's quiet competence. Jude insists he is a tradesman, not a maker of history. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by restlessness.

chapters.title: Rumors from the Capital
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. News arrives of unrest in the capital; the townsfolk dismiss it as distant noise. Elodie listens too closely, Jude notices. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in the belief that history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Winter floods and military orders close the bridge — the only road out — until spring. Jude, who planned to leave for the capital, is stranded. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and thwarted ambition.

chapters.title: What Elodie Cuts After Midnight
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She secretly cuts rebel type at night and hides plates beneath the floorboards. The reader learns the workshop serves two masters. Emotional beat: fear braided with fierce purpose.

chapters.title: The Soldier at the Counter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A garrison officer commissions printed proclamations; Jude must set type for lies he half-believes. Emotional beat: complicity, the first taste of moral compromise.

chapters.title: A Ledger of the Missing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A widow brings a list of villagers taken by soldiers and begs the Sterlings to print the truth. Elodie agrees in secret. Emotional beat: grief transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: Apprentice to Two Masters
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude discovers Elodie's hidden press run. Instead of denouncing her, he is drawn in — and begins setting type for the resistance by night. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of chosen allegiance.

chapters.title: The Currency of Lies
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. Ambrose knows more than he says; he prints for the regime to keep the workshop alive, believing survival is the only justice available to small men. Emotional beat: weary pragmatism cracking under guilt.

chapters.title: First Distribution
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The first truth-pamphlets go out hidden in bread deliveries. Jude sees a farmer read his typeset words and weep. Emotional beat: the shocking intimacy of one's work changing a stranger.

chapters.title: The Raid That Missed
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Soldiers search the workshop on a tip; the hidden plates survive by minutes. Elodie realizes there is an informer. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a press screw.

chapters.title: Informer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude deduces the informer is the workshop's delivery boy, bribed and frightened. Confronting him means becoming judge outside any law. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — justice without courts.

chapters.title: Ambrose Taken
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Soldiers arrest Ambrose for treason, seizing his correspondence. The workshop is marked for confiscation when the thaw comes. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of everything.

chapters.title: What the Father Left
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie finds her father's secret testament — evidence of the massacres, dictated and hidden in a locked type case — unfinished, missing its final pages. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden and weapon.

chapters.title: The Last Pages
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The missing pages are with the imprisoned Ambrose. Jude volunteers to smuggle a message in via printed handbill, risking arrest himself. Emotional beat: courage discovered in motion.

chapters.title: Through the Prison Wall
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The handbill gambit half-succeeds: Ambrose sends the final pages out sewn in a blanket, but the garrison learns the workshop is the resistance's press. Emotional beat: hope and countdown intertwined.

chapters.title: The Thaw Begins
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ice cracks on the river; the bridge will open — and with it, the soldiers' reinforcements and the workshop's destruction. Time runs out in earnest. Emotional beat: dread sharpening every hour.

chapters.title: Setting the Truth by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A sleepless night of composition: the full record of the massacres, set in the finest type Ambrose ever cut. Elodie and Jude work as one. Emotional beat: tenderness and urgency fused.

chapters.title: The Presses at Midnight
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The print run begins as soldiers march on the workshop. Pages fly; the town wakes to paper on every doorstep. Emotional beat: triumph at the edge of catastrophe.

chapters.title: Fire
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The garrison burns the workshop; Elodie and Jude save the type case and the last copies, fleeing through the smoke as the presses die. Emotional beat: loss and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Town That Read
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The pamphlet spreads; the garrison, named and shamed, withdraws rather than massacre a town that knows. Ambrose is freed by the crowd. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, achieved by memory made print.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Spring, the bridge passable at last. Jude can leave — everything he wanted — but the town, the work, and Elodie have remade what he wants. Emotional beat: choice replacing circumstance.

chapters.title: Compositor
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating. Jude and Elodie cross the bridge carrying the type case, bound for a new press in the capital, no longer spectators to history but its hands. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won hope.
